p.src: This Lady Li was the wife of Jia Zhu. Although Zhu had died young, he had fortunately left a son named Jia Lan, who was now five years old and had already begun his schooling. Lady Li herself was the daughter of a distinguished official family of Jinling. Her father, Li Shouzhong, had once served as Chancellor of the Imperial Academy, and there was neither man nor woman in the clan who did not read poetry and study the classics. But when Li Shouzhong inherited the headship of the family, he began to maintain that “lack of learning is a virtue in a woman.” Thus, after his daughter was born, he did not have her study very much. He merely let her read three or four works such as The Four Books for Women, Biographies of Exemplary Women, and Collected Lives of Worthy Ladies, so that she might recognize a few characters and remember the names of several virtuous women of former dynasties. He regarded spinning, weaving, and household labor as the essentials. She was therefore named Li Wan, with the courtesy name Gongcai. Consequently, although Li Wan had lost her husband in the bloom of youth and lived amid every luxury of fine food and splendid silks, she was like withered wood and dead ashes, blind and deaf to everything around her. She devoted herself solely to serving her elders and raising her son, and otherwise merely accompanied her young sisters-in-law in their needlework and reading. Thus, though Daiyu was living here as a guest, she had such companions with her every day; apart from concern for her aged father, there was nothing else she needed to worry about.

p.src: Let us now return to Yucun. Upon being reinstated as Prefect of Yingtian, no sooner had he taken office than a homicide case was submitted for his judgment. Two families had fought over the purchase of a maidservant, neither yielding to the other, until the brawl ended in a death. Yucun immediately summoned the plaintiff for questioning. The plaintiff said, “The man beaten to death was my master. That day he bought a girl, not knowing that she had been abducted and put up for sale by a kidnapper. The kidnapper had already taken our family's silver, but our young master said that the third day would be auspicious and that he would bring her home then. But the kidnapper secretly sold her again to the Xue family. When we learned of it, we went to seize the seller and recover the girl. Unfortunately, the Xue family is a tyrannical power in Jinling. Relying on its wealth and influence, its brutal servants beat my young master to death. The murderer and his servants have all fled without a trace, leaving behind only a few people who had no part in the affair. I have petitioned the authorities for a whole year, yet no one has given us justice. I beg Your Excellency to arrest the criminals, root out the evildoers, and deliver the orphan and widow from their plight. Then the dead man himself will be eternally grateful for Heaven's grace!”

p.src: Yucun flew into a rage on hearing this. “What outrageous nonsense is this! Can a man be beaten to death and his killers simply walk away, never to be caught?” He was about to issue warrants ordering the constables to arrest and interrogate members of the culprit's clan at once, forcing them to reveal where he was hidden, while also circulating a general proclamation for his capture. Just as he was about to issue the warrants, he noticed a yamen attendant standing beside the bench signaling with his eyes that he should not do so. Yucun found this exceedingly strange, but could only stay his hand. He immediately adjourned the court and withdrew to a private chamber, dismissing all his attendants except the gatekeeper, whom he kept to wait upon him. The gatekeeper hurried forward to pay his respects and asked with a smile, “Your Excellency has risen steadily in rank and fortune. Have you forgotten me after eight or nine years?” Yucun replied, “Your face is extremely familiar, but for the moment I cannot place you.” The gatekeeper laughed. “Your Excellency truly has the short memory of a great man! You have even forgotten the place from which you first set forth. Do you not remember what happened years ago at the Bottle-Gourd Temple?” At these words Yucun started as though struck by thunder, and only then did he recall the past. It turned out that the gatekeeper had once been a young novice at the Bottle-Gourd Temple. After the fire left him with nowhere to live, he had thought of entering another temple to continue his religious life, but could not endure its cold and austere conditions. Deciding that a yamen post would be easier and livelier, he had taken advantage of his youth to grow out his hair and become a gatekeeper. Yucun had never imagined it could be he. He hastily took his hand and said with a smile, “So it is an old friend!” He then invited him to sit down so that they might talk at leisure. The gatekeeper did not dare to sit. Yucun smiled. “One must never forget the friends one knew in humble days. You and I are old acquaintances, and besides, this is a private chamber. Since we mean to talk at length, how could you possibly remain standing?” Hearing this, the gatekeeper thanked him for the seat and perched sideways on its edge.

p.src: Yucun then asked why he had signaled him not to issue the warrants. The gatekeeper replied, “Now that Your Excellency has obtained this distinguished appointment in this province, surely you have copied out a ‘Talisman for the Protection of Officials’ for the province?” Yucun hastily asked, “What is this ‘Talisman for the Protection of Officials’? I know nothing of it.” The gatekeeper said, “This is serious! If you do not even know this, how can you hope to remain in office for long? Nowadays every local official keeps a private list bearing the names of the most powerful, influential, immensely rich, and exalted great families in his province. It is the same in every province. If an official is ignorant of the list and inadvertently offends one of these families, he will not only lose his rank; he may not even be able to preserve his life! That is why it has been nicknamed the ‘Talisman for the Protection of Officials.’ How could Your Excellency possibly provoke the Xue family just mentioned? There is nothing difficult about judging this case; it has remained unresolved only because every official is constrained by personal ties and considerations of face.” As he spoke, he drew a copied ‘Talisman for the Protection of Officials’ from his document pouch and handed it to Yucun. On inspection, it proved to contain popular sayings about the leading clans and eminent official families of the locality. The sayings were set out clearly, with notes beneath each one recording the offices and titles held by the founding ancestor and the various branches of the family. p.src: Yucun had not yet finished reading when he suddenly heard the caller's clapper, and a servant announced, “His Excellency Wang has come to pay a visit.” On hearing this, Yucun hurriedly put on his formal robes and cap and went out to receive him. It was the time it takes to eat a meal before he returned and resumed his careful questioning. The attendant said, “These four families are all bound together by marriage. If one suffers, they all suffer; if one prospers, they all prosper. They support and shield one another, and each can rely upon the others. The Xue accused of beating a man to death is none other than the ‘snow’ in ‘a great snowfall in a bountiful year.’ Nor does he depend on those other three families alone; he has no small number of old family friends and relatives, both in the capital and elsewhere. Whom, then, does Your Excellency propose to arrest?” Hearing this, Yucun smiled and asked the attendant, “If matters are as you say, how is this case to be settled? I suppose you also know very well where the murderer has fled?”

p.src: The attendant smiled. “To tell Your Excellency the truth, I know not only where the murderer went, but also the kidnapper who sold the girl and the buyer who is now dead. Let me explain it all to Your Excellency. The man who was beaten to death was the son of a minor local gentleman. His name was Feng Yuan. His parents died when he was young, and he had no brothers, so he lived alone on a modest inheritance. By the age of eighteen or nineteen, he was passionately devoted to men and detested women above all things. It must have been some ill-fated bond from a former life: by chance he encountered the kidnapper offering this girl for sale and fell for her at first sight. He resolved to buy her as his concubine and swore that he would have no more dealings with men and would never take another woman. That was why she was not to enter his household until three days later. But who could have known that the kidnapper would secretly sell her again to the Xue family? He meant to pocket the silver from both parties and then flee to another province. Instead, he failed to get away. The two parties seized him and beat him within an inch of his life. Neither would take back the silver; each demanded the girl. Young Master Xue was hardly a man to yield. He ordered his servants to attack, and they beat Young Master Feng to a pulp. Feng was carried home and died three days later. Young Master Xue had already chosen a date for his journey to the capital. Two days before his departure, he happened upon this girl and intended to buy her and then proceed to the capital. Who could have expected such a disturbance to arise? After having Feng beaten and seizing the girl, he carried on as though nothing had happened and simply set off on his journey with his household. He has brothers and servants here to manage the affair. Such a trifling matter would hardly be worth fleeing over. But let that pass. Who do you suppose the girl being sold was, Your Excellency?” Yucun smiled. “How should I know?” The attendant gave a cold laugh. “As it happens, she is the daughter of your great benefactor! She is Yinglian, the daughter of Master Zhen, who lived beside the Gourd Temple.” Yucun exclaimed in astonishment, “So it was she! I heard that she was kidnapped at the age of five. Why has she only now been put up for sale?”

p.src: The attendant replied, “Kidnappers of this kind make a practice of abducting children of five or six and raising them in some secluded place. When they reach eleven or twelve, the kidnappers judge their looks and take them to another region to be resold. In those days we played with Yinglian every day. Though seven or eight years have passed and she is now about twelve or thirteen, and though she has grown considerably prettier and more graceful, her general features have naturally not changed, so anyone who knew her could easily recognize her. Besides, she had from birth a rouge-colored mole the size of a grain of rice between her brows. That is how I recognized her. As fate would have it, the kidnapper had rented a room from me. One day when he was away, I questioned her myself. She had been so terrified by his beatings that she dared not reveal a word. She said only that the kidnapper was her own father and was selling her because he had no money to repay his debts. I coaxed her again and again, but she merely began to cry and said, ‘I remember nothing from when I was little!’ That left no room for doubt. On the day Young Master Feng inspected her and paid over the silver, the kidnapper became drunk, and she sighed to herself, ‘Today my burden of sin has surely come to an end!’ Later, when she heard that Young Master Feng had ordered that she be brought to his household three days afterward, she became anxious again. I could not bear to see her in such a state. When the kidnapper went out, I had my wife comfort her: ‘Young Master Feng insists on waiting for an auspicious day before he comes to receive you, which shows that he certainly does not regard you as a mere servant girl. Moreover, he is a man of exceptional refinement and good looks, his household is comfortably situated, and he has always detested women. Now he has paid an extraordinary price for you; what will follow needs no saying. You need only endure another two or three days. Why be so distressed?’ Only after hearing this was her anxiety somewhat relieved, for she believed that at last she had found a proper home. Who could have imagined that such bitter disappointments exist in this world? The very next day, the kidnapper sold her to the Xue family as well. Had she been sold to anyone else, it might still have been bearable. But Young Master Xue is nicknamed the ‘Foolish Tyrant.’ No man under heaven is more violent or quick-tempered, and he scatters money like dirt. He had Feng's party thoroughly beaten and dragged Yinglian away by brute force. Whether she is alive or dead now, no one knows. Young Master Feng's joy came to nothing. His one desire went unfulfilled, and instead he spent his money and lost his life. Is that not lamentable?”

p.src: Yucun listened and sighed. “Their meeting was born of karmic affliction and was no mere accident. Otherwise, why should Feng Yuan have set his heart on Yinglian alone? After suffering at the kidnapper’s hands for all these years, Yinglian had at last found a way out; and since Feng Yuan was a man of deep feeling, their union might have been a happy one. Yet this calamity had to arise. Though the Xue family is richer and nobler than the Fengs, judging by Xue Pan’s character he must have numerous concubines and indulge his lust without restraint. He can hardly compare with Feng Yuan, whose affections were fixed on one woman alone. It is truly a dreamlike romance in which two ill-fated young people happened to meet. But let us speak no more of them. How should the present case be decided?” The attendant laughed. “How wise and decisive Your Honour was in former days! Why have you become so irresolute today? I hear that Your Honour owes your appointment to this post to the influence of the Jia and Wang families. Xue Pan is a relative of the Jias, so why not go with the current, do them a generous favour, and bring this case to a close? That will also make it easier for you to face the Jia and Wang families in future.” “What you say is certainly true,” replied Yucun. But a human life is at stake. By His Majesty’s boundless grace, I was restored to office and entrusted with this post; it was as though I had been given a new life. At this very time, when I ought to devote all my heart and strength to repaying that grace, how could I set the law aside for private interests? That is something I truly cannot bring myself to do.” The attendant gave a cold laugh. “What Your Honour says is undoubtedly a lofty principle, but it simply cannot be put into practice in the world as it is today. Have you not heard the ancients say, ‘A true man acts according to the times,’ and also, ‘He who seeks good fortune and avoids calamity is a gentleman’? If you act as you have just said, not only will you be unable to serve the court, but you will fail to preserve even yourself. You would do well to think it over carefully.”

p.src: Yucun lowered his head for a long while before saying, “Then what do you propose?” The attendant replied, “I have already devised an excellent plan. When Your Honour takes your seat in court tomorrow, make a great show of authority and issue warrants and summonses for arrests. Naturally, the principal culprit cannot be caught, though the plaintiffs will certainly insist that several members and servants of the Xue clan be arrested and examined under torture. I shall mediate in secret and have the Xues report that he died suddenly of an illness. His clansmen and the local authorities will jointly submit a certified statement. Your Honour need only claim to be skilled at invoking immortals by planchette, set up a divination altar in the court, and allow soldiers and commoners alike to come and watch. Then Your Honour can announce: ‘The divining immortal has pronounced that the dead Feng Yuan and Xue Pan met because of karmic debts from a former life. Having now encountered each other in a narrow pass, they were destined to settle that debt. Xue Pan has now contracted a mysterious illness and died, pursued by Feng Yuan’s vengeful spirit. The entire calamity was caused by a certain kidnapper, a man of such-and-such a surname from such-and-such a village. He is to be punished according to law, while no one else shall be implicated,’ or words to that effect. Meanwhile, I shall secretly instruct the kidnapper to make a full confession. When everyone sees that the immortal’s pronouncement agrees with the kidnapper’s confession, they will naturally believe that the rest is true as well. The Xues have money in abundance. Your Honour may order them to pay a thousand taels, or five hundred, to the Feng family for funeral expenses. There is no one of consequence in the Feng family, and money is all they are after. Once they have the silver, I imagine they will have nothing more to say. Consider it carefully, Your Honour. What do you think of this plan?” Yucun smiled. “No, no, that will not do. Let me consider it further. Perhaps we can find a way to silence public criticism.” By the time the two had finished their deliberations, it was already late, and nothing further was said.

u.src: Yucun lowered his head for a long while before saying, “Then what do you propose?”
The attendant replied, “I have already devised an excellent plan. When Your Honour takes your seat in court tomorrow, make a great show of authority and issue warrants and summonses for arrests.
Naturally, the principal culprit cannot be caught, though the plaintiffs will certainly insist that several members and servants of the Xue clan be arrested and examined under torture.

I shall mediate in secret and have the Xues report that he died suddenly of an illness. His clansmen and the local authorities will jointly submit a certified statement. Your Honour need only claim to be skilled at invoking immortals by planchette, set up a divination altar in the court, and allow soldiers and commoners alike to come and watch.

Then Your Honour can announce: ‘The divining immortal has pronounced that the dead Feng Yuan and Xue Pan met because of karmic debts from a former life. Having now encountered each other in a narrow pass, they were destined to settle that debt.
Xue Pan has now contracted a mysterious illness and died, pursued by Feng Yuan’s vengeful spirit.

The entire calamity was caused by a certain kidnapper, a man of such-and-such a surname from such-and-such a village. He is to be punished according to law, while no one else shall be implicated,’ or words to that effect.
Meanwhile, I shall secretly instruct the kidnapper to make a full confession.
When everyone sees that the immortal’s pronouncement agrees with the kidnapper’s confession, they will naturally believe that the rest is true as well.

Consider it carefully, Your Honour. What do you think of this plan?”
Yucun smiled. “No, no, that will not do.
Let me consider it further. Perhaps we can find a way to silence public criticism.”
By the time the two had finished their deliberations, it was already late, and nothing further was said.

p.src: The next day, when court convened, all the named parties were summoned. Yucun questioned them closely and found, just as expected, that the Feng family had few members and was merely using the case to obtain more funeral money, while the Xues, relying on their power and connections, stubbornly refused to yield. Thus the case had remained tangled and undecided. Yucun then bent the law for private favour and disposed of the case with a muddled judgment. Having received a considerable sum for funeral expenses, the Feng family had nothing more to say. As soon as Yucun had settled the case, he hurriedly wrote two letters, one to Jia Zheng and the other to Wang Ziteng, Commander of the Capital Garrison. They said little more than, “The matter concerning your nephew has been settled; there is no need for further concern.” The whole scheme had originated with the former novice of the Gourd Temple, now serving as the new attendant. Yucun feared that the man might tell others of his poverty and low estate in earlier days, and the thought greatly troubled him. In the end, he found some fault with the attendant and had him banished far away, after which he finally let the matter rest.

p.src: For the moment, we shall say no more of Yucun. Let us instead speak of Young Master Xue, who had bought Yinglian and beaten Feng Yuan to death. He too was a native of Jinling and came from a family of scholars extending back through generations. But Young Master Xue had lost his father in childhood, and his widowed mother, cherishing him as her sole heir, inevitably spoiled and indulged him. Thus he grew to manhood without accomplishing anything. His family, moreover, possessed a fortune of a million and held an imperial commission to draw funds from the privy treasury and procure miscellaneous supplies. This young gentleman's formal name was Xue Pan and his courtesy name Wenqi. From the age of five he had been extravagant by nature and arrogant in speech. Though he had attended school, he had learned scarcely more than a few characters, and spent his days doing nothing but fighting cocks, racing horses, roaming the hills, and amusing himself by the waters. Although he was an imperial merchant, he knew absolutely nothing of business or worldly affairs. He merely relied on the connections left by his grandfather, held a nominal post at the Ministry of Revenue, and drew its funds and provisions; all other matters were managed by clerks and old family servants. His widowed mother, née Wang, was the younger sister of Wang Ziteng, the current Commander of the Capital Garrison, and the full sister of Lady Wang, wife of Jia Zheng of the Rongguo House. She was then about forty years old and had only one son, Xue Pan. She also had a daughter, two years younger than Xue Pan, whose childhood name was Baochai. The girl was fair and graceful in form, and gentle and refined in manner. While her father was alive, he had doted on this daughter and taught her to read and write; in ability she proved fully ten times superior to her elder brother. After her father's death, however, she saw that her brother could not comfort or support their mother, so she ceased to make books and writing her chief concern and devoted herself instead to needlework and household management, hoping to share her mother's worries and lighten her burdens. Recently, because the present Emperor esteemed poetry and honored the rites and wished to recruit the talented, he had bestowed an unprecedented favor: besides selecting imperial consorts and concubines, daughters of officials and distinguished families were all to have their names submitted personally to the ministry, so that they might be chosen to attend princesses of the imperial and princely ranks in their studies and serve in the offices of Talented Lady or Mentor of Virtue. A second consideration was that, since Xue Pan's father had died, the agents, managers, and clerks conducting the family's business in the various provinces had seen that Xue Pan was young and ignorant of worldly affairs and had taken the opportunity to swindle him; even the several businesses in the capital were gradually declining. Xue Pan had long heard that the capital was the most splendid and prosperous place in the realm and had been eager to visit it. He therefore seized this opportunity: first, to escort his sister there for selection; second, to visit relatives; and third, to present himself at the ministry to settle the old accounts and arrange new disbursements. His true intention, however, was to enjoy the sights and splendors of the imperial capital. He had therefore already prepared the luggage and valuables for the journey, together with all manner of local products and gifts for relatives and friends, and was choosing an auspicious day for his certain departure when, unexpectedly, he happened upon the kidnapper trying to sell Yinglian a second time. Seeing that Yinglian was no ordinary beauty, Xue Pan resolved to buy her. When the Feng household came to claim her, he relied on his power and ordered his brutal servants to beat Feng Yuan to death. He then entrusted every item of household business to members of his clan and several old family servants, and set out directly on the long journey with his mother and sister.

p.src: As for the murder case, he treated it as mere child's play, believing that there was nothing a few filthy coins could not settle.

p.src: How many days they spent on the road need not be recorded. On the day they were about to enter the capital, they heard that his maternal uncle Wang Ziteng had been promoted to Commander-in-Chief of the Nine Provinces and, by imperial command, had left the capital to inspect the frontier. Xue Pan rejoiced inwardly: “I was just worried that once I reached the capital, my own maternal uncle would keep me under his thumb and prevent me from spending as freely as I pleased. And now, of all times, he has been promoted and sent away. Clearly Heaven grants a man's wishes.” He therefore consulted his mother: “Although we own several residences in the capital, no one from our family has lived there for a dozen years or so. The caretakers have probably been renting them out secretly, so we had better send a few men ahead to clean and put them in order.” His mother replied, “Why make such a display? Now that we have come to the capital, we ought first to call upon our relatives and friends and stay either at your uncle's house or at your aunt and her husband's. Both houses have ample accommodation. We can stay there first and then have our own residences put in order at leisure. Would that not be much easier?” Xue Pan said, “Uncle is being transferred to the provinces just now, so his household will naturally be in turmoil preparing to leave. If the whole crowd of us descended upon them at such a time, would that not be terribly inconsiderate?” His mother said, “Even if your uncle's family is leaving for his new post, there is still your aunt and her husband's household. Besides, in recent years both your uncle's and your aunt's households have repeatedly sent messages and letters inviting us to come. Now that we have arrived, although your uncle is busy preparing to depart, your aunt in the Jia family will surely urge us to stay. If we hurried off at once to prepare our own residences, would people not take offense? I know very well what you have in mind: living under the eyes of your uncle or your aunt's husband would cramp your freedom, whereas if you lived apart, you could do whatever you pleased. Since that is how you feel, you may choose a residence for yourself. Your aunt and I are sisters who have been apart for several years, and I intend to spend some days with her. I shall take your sister to your aunt's house. What do you say to that?” Seeing his mother speak in this manner, Xue Pan knew he could not prevail upon her. He had no choice but to order the porters to proceed directly to the Rongguo House.

p.src: By then Lady Wang had already learned of Xue Pan's murder case and knew that, thanks to Jia Yucun's intervention, it had been settled; only then had she set her mind at ease. Then, seeing that her elder brother had been promoted to a frontier post, she was just lamenting that there would be one fewer relative from her own family with whom to associate and was feeling somewhat lonely. Several days later, a servant suddenly announced, “Her Ladyship your sister has arrived in the capital with the young master and young lady and the whole household. They are alighting from their carriages outside the gate.” Delighted, Lady Wang hurriedly gathered the women of the family and the daughters-in-law, went out as far as the main hall to receive them, and escorted Aunt Xue and the others inside. The sisters, reunited in their later years, were naturally overcome by mingled sorrow and joy; weeping and laughing, they spoke at length of all that had happened during their separation. They were then promptly conducted to pay their respects to Grandmother Jia, and presented all manner of gifts and local products. After everyone in the family had exchanged greetings, a banquet was hastily prepared to welcome the travelers.

p.src: After Xue Pan had paid his respects to Jia Zheng, Jia Lian took him to call upon Jia She, Jia Zhen, and the others. Jia Zheng then sent someone to tell Lady Wang, “Your sister is already advanced in years, while your nephew is young and knows little of the ways of the world. If they live outside, I fear someone may stir up trouble. In our northeast corner stands Pear-Fragrance Court, with some ten rooms lying entirely vacant. It would be excellent to have it cleaned and invite your sister, her daughter, and her son to live there.” Before Lady Wang had time to press them to stay, Grandmother Jia also sent someone with such messages as, “Please ask your sister to settle here, so that we may all be closer.” Aunt Xue herself wished to live with the family, for only then could she keep a tighter rein on her son; if they lived elsewhere, she feared he would indulge his unruly nature and bring disaster upon himself. She therefore hastened to give thanks and accept. She also privately made it clear to Lady Wang, “We must be excused from all provision for our daily expenses; only then can we live here on an ordinary, lasting footing.” Lady Wang knew that such expenses presented no difficulty to the Xue family, and so consented to her wish. From that time onward, the Xue family—mother and children—lived in Pear-Fragrance Court.

p.src: Pear-Fragrance Court, as it happened, was where Lord Rong had retired to peace and quiet in his later years. Small and exquisitely laid out, it contained a little over ten rooms, complete with a front hall and rear quarters. It also had a separate gate opening onto the street, which the Xue household’s servants used for coming and going. At the southwest stood a side gate leading into a narrow passage; emerging from the passage brought one to the east side of Lady Wang’s main apartments. Every day, either after meals or in the evening, Aunt Xue would come over, sometimes to chat with Grandmother Jia and sometimes to visit with Lady Wang. Baochai spent her days with Daiyu, Yingchun, and the other girls, reading or playing chess, or else doing needlework, and found herself quite happily occupied. Xue Pan alone had originally been unwilling to live in the Jia mansion, fearing that his uncle would discipline and restrain him and that life there would surely be uncomfortable. But since his mother was determined to remain, while the household pressed them most warmly to stay, he had no choice but to settle there for the time being, intending meanwhile to have his own house put in order and move back once it was ready. Who could have known that, before he had lived there even a month, he would already be acquainted with half the younger members of the Jia clan? Every one of the pampered idlers among them delighted in his company: one day they held a drinking party, the next they went to admire flowers, and soon they were gathering to gamble and frequenting prostitutes, gradually stopping at no vice whatever. Under their influence, Xue Pan became ten times worse than he had been before. Although Jia Zheng knew how to instruct his sons and govern his household, the clan was so large and its members so numerous that he could not keep watch over all these young men. Moreover, the present head of the clan was Jia Zhen, the eldest grandson of the Ning branch, who had inherited its title and was naturally responsible for clan affairs. Besides, Jia Zheng was encumbered with both official and domestic business, and by temperament was free and easy, attaching little importance to mundane matters. Whenever he had leisure from public duties, he did no more than read or play chess, and paid scant attention to anything else. Furthermore, Pear-Fragrance Court was separated from the main residence by two ranges of buildings and had its own street gate, through which anyone could come and go at will. These young men could therefore indulge themselves without restraint, and Xue Pan’s intention of moving away gradually faded altogether.
